title: Enforce the operational stored contract without historical reinterpretation
statement: The Operational record persistence Module shall accept only the declared current v3 stored contract for operational record access, candidate validation, publication, and recovery, and reject retired, unknown, mixed, or cross-version input without conversion, fallback, or historical-byte modification.

what.problem: An operational reader or recovery path can silently restore withdrawn stored-format support even when command admission rejects it.
what.desired_outcome: Every persistence entry path enforces the same current stored boundary while historical content retains its original meaning.

why.rationale: SR-040 requires stored-contract rejection behind public dispatch; MOD-011 owns the records and recovery state that must enforce it.

stakeholders: Engineers and agents supplying explicit command requests
Maintainers of MOD-011 and its Interface consumers

conditions: A current store, creation candidate, replacement, or recovery journal reaches an operational-record entry point.

contexts: The IF-003 operational-record boundary and the selected store, candidates, and recovery material it governs.

how.approach: Check explicit stored discriminators and the applicable journal contract before operational interpretation; keep this selection independent from public transport and document versions.

how_much.scope: The exact current and retired stored populations named in CLI and Record Format. Bounded archive recognition for discovery remains classification, not a historical record validator or operational reader.

acceptance_criteria: A new operational store identifies contract rigorloop-records-v3 on its change manifest; that manifest and every registered supporting record use stored schema_version 3. Supporting records are not required to repeat the manifest's contract field, and a transport or model-document version never substitutes for the applicable stored discriminator.

Retired or unknown contracts, unsupported stored versions, mixed registered records, and cross-version replacements receive their declared safe rejection with no authoritative write, conversion, fallback reader, or inferred renewed authority.
An unsupported or retired journal cannot trigger recovery or operational continuation; inspection and rejected access do not alter historical bytes, identities, or meaning.

The same stored support boundary applies to targeted candidates, advanced complete-byte replacements, and explicit recovery, while independently supported transport and shared-definition versions remain usable under their own contracts.

sources.basis: Derive this draft lower-level obligation from the containing SR at the selected command or operational-record responsibility boundary. Allocation and acceptance criteria are design claims for review, not implementation, requirement approval, or satisfaction evidence.

sources.locator: docs/design/cli/cli.md#CLI-SR-10, CLI-SR-27, CLI-SR-28; docs/design/cli/records.md#RF-SR-01, RF-SR-06, RF-SR-09, RF-SR-12, RF-SR-14
sources.basis: Preserve the applicable current public and stored-record guarantees at this accountable boundary. The named source retains exact schemas, operation tables, classifications, limits, and historical adoption obligations; this allocation neither replaces those details nor accepts REM authoring JSON as operational records.
